system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: USM allocation types

ATOM DPCPP2-C06-S3-03 (S3): Although shared allocations can migrate, not all SYCL implementations necessarily migrate them; some devices may implement them identically to host allocations, so they remain visible on host and device but may not show the performance gains of migration.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0184-s05] We should also note that while shared allocations can migrate, it does
[DPCPP2-p0184-s06] not necessarily mean that all implementations of SYCL will migrate them.
[DPCPP2-p0184-s07] We expect most implementations to implement shared allocations with migration, but some devices may prefer to implement them identically to host allocations.
[DPCPP2-p0184-s08] In such an implementation, the allocation is still visible on both host and device, but we may not see the performance gains that a migrating implementation could provide.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Combines optional migration, implementation as host allocations, host/device visibility, and possible absence of migration-related performance gains. / Joins multiple claims: migration is optional across implementations, shared allocations can be implemented as host allocations, and the resulting visibility/performance trade-off.
- L1_ONLY: revise — Retain the recall-level fact that shared allocations need not migrate; remove the additional implementation, visibility, and performance clauses. / Carries extra load from stacked clauses (Although..., some..., so... but...) that should be trimmed to one core fact.
